title: Scaling cross-situational word learning on children's naturalistic experiences
abstract: arXiv:2610.31842v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How do children learn the meanings of the simple, concrete words that form a majority of their early vocabulary? Statistical information about many word meanings can be recovered from the gradual accumulation of information about the co-occurrence of words with their referents, a proposal known as ``cross-situational learning''. Contrastive vision--language models allow this learning strategy to be tested on egocentric video data capturing children's early real-life experiences with visual and linguistic inputs. Initial successes of this method on small datasets provide a proof-of-concept, but vision models struggle to learn robust visual representations when trained on these same egocentric videos. How dependent is cross-situational word learning performance on the quality of the model's visual representations? And can cross-situational models scale to larger and more diverse datasets? translated_title: 在儿童自然经验数据上扩展跨情境词汇学习
translated_abstract: 儿童是如何学习那些构成其早期词汇大部分的简单、具体词汇的含义的？关于许多词义的统计信息可以通过逐步积累词汇与其指称对象共现的信息来获得，这一理论被称为“跨情境学习”。对比式视觉-语言模型使这一学习策略能够在捕捉儿童早期真实生活经验（包含视觉和语言输入）的第一人称视角视频数据上进行测试。该方法在小型数据集上的初步成功提供了概念验证，但视觉模型在这些同样的第一人称视频上训练时难以学到鲁棒的视觉表征。跨情境词汇学习的表现在多大程度上依赖于模型视觉表征的质量？跨情境模型能否扩展到更大、更多样化的数据集？为了回答这些问题，我们在……
tldr: 该研究探讨了基于儿童自然第一人称视频经验的跨情境词汇学习能否规模化，重点考察其表现对视觉表征质量的依赖性以及在更大、更多样化数据集上的扩展能力。
en_tdlr: This study investigates whether cross-situational word learning can scale on children's naturalistic egocentric video experiences, examining how performance depends on visual representation quality and whether models can generalize to larger, more diverse datasets.
